title: Reply: superstition hides mysteries — Christian truth is not ashamed
source_text: XXXIII. Respondeo, proprium esse superstitionis occultare sua mysteria, & plebem ab eis arcere, ut Ethnici olim faciebant. Sed religionem Christianam sui ipsius non pudet; ac, ut ait Tertullianus, veritas Christi nihil erubescit nisi abscondi. Itaque religio Christiana nemini sui notitiam invidet, sed ad eam ipsos infideles invitat. Fateor quidem hac in re prudentia aliqua opus esse. Nam monet Christus sanctum non esse dandum canibus, nec margaritas porcis objiciendas esse. Aliter etiam agendum cum parvulis in Christo, aliter cum perfectis. Et prioribus quidem lac praebendum est, posterioribus, cibus solidus reservandus. Itaque Pastorum atque Doctorum est hac in re auditorum suorum rationem habere, & doctrinam Evangelii, quam ex Scripturis hauriunt, dextre & ad captum eorum, qui audiunt, proponere, nec temere religionis Christianae mysteria profanis & impiis ridenda exponere. Sed contra prudentiam istam, a Christo ipso praeceptam, non peccarunt Evangelistae & Apostoli nostri, dum integrum Evangelium breviter & summatim scriptis suis consignarunt. Nam illa ipsa scripta proponi & exponi possunt aliis ad modum lactis, aliis vero ad modum solidioris cibi. Neque quicquid scriptum est, protinus censeri debet porcis objectum esse, & profanorum sibilis & cachinnis expositum. Alioquin ipsi Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae sanctum canibus quotidie darent, & margaritas porcis objicerent, si quidem illi quotidie Theologicas summas, & Catecheses edunt, & religionis Christianae mysteria quaelibet scripto docent, & explicant, quam clare & aperte possunt. Quod certe si ipsis licet, inviolata manente dignitate mysteriorum Evangelicorum, cur idem non licuerit Apostolis & Evangelistis? Si vero non licuit, nec decuit Apostolos scripto explicare omnia fidei mysteria, cur idem hodie magis licebit scholasticis & Theologis Pontificiis, qui omnia Pontificiae Theologiae dogmata scripto docent, & illa ipsa, quae dicit Bellarminus, tremenda Missae mysteria, quorum nullum prorsus est quod scriptum non reperiatur in Pontificiorum libris.
pass_a_gloss: I answer, it is proper to superstition to hide its mysteries, and to keep the people away from them, as the pagans once did. But the Christian religion is not ashamed of itself; and, as Tertullian says, the truth of Christ blushes at nothing except being hidden. Therefore the Christian religion begrudges no one knowledge of itself, but invites the unbelievers themselves to it. I confess indeed that some prudence is needed in this matter. For Christ warns that what is holy is not to be given to dogs, nor are pearls to be cast before swine. One must also act otherwise with babes in Christ, otherwise with the perfect. And to the former milk is to be offered, to the latter solid food is to be reserved. Therefore it belongs to Pastors and Doctors in this matter to take account of their hearers, and to propose the doctrine of the Gospel, which they draw from the Scriptures, skillfully and to the capacity of those who hear, and not rashly to expose the mysteries of the Christian religion to the profane and impious to be mocked. But against that prudence, commanded by Christ himself, our Evangelists and Apostles did not sin, when they briefly and summarily committed the whole Gospel to their writings. For those very writings can be proposed and expounded to some after the manner of milk, to others truly after the manner of more solid food. Nor ought whatever is written straightway be judged cast before swine, and exposed to the hisses and laughter of the profane. Otherwise the Doctors of the Roman Church themselves would daily give what is holy to dogs, and cast pearls before swine, if indeed they daily publish theological summas and catechisms, and teach and explain any mysteries of the Christian religion in writing, as clearly and openly as they can. Which certainly, if it is permitted to them, the dignity of the Evangelical mysteries remaining inviolate, why would the same not have been permitted to the Apostles and Evangelists? But if it was not permitted, nor fitting, for the Apostles to explain all the mysteries of the faith in writing, why will the same today be more permitted to scholastic and Pontifical theologians, who teach all the dogmas of Pontifical theology in writing, and those very tremendous mysteries of the Mass of which Bellarmine speaks, of which there is absolutely none that is not found written in the books of the Pontificii.
pass_b_english: Reply: hiding mysteries is superstition's habit — pagans barred the crowd.
Christian truth is not ashamed; Tertullian: it blushes only at being hidden.
Prudence still holds — milk for babes, solid food for the mature; do not cast pearls.
Writing the Gospel is not casting pearls: Rome's own summas and catechisms already publish every Mass mystery Bellarmine calls tremendous.
